output.summary: KEP-1602 proposes a standard structure for Kubernetes log messages, new klog methods (InfoS, ErrorS) and helpers to enforce that structure, a JSON log output option for components, and an incremental migration to structured logging. Its status is implementable at stage beta.
output.rationale:
Current control-plane logs have no uniform structure and object references, so parsing and analysis rely on ad-hoc regular expressions. The KEP adds klog methods to enforce structure and a JSON output format, while keeping klog and limiting migration to a scope SIG-instrumentation can execute. Full migration of all logs is explicitly out of scope.</ser_rationale>
<parameter name="outcome_reason">null

alternatives.option: Just write guidelines and update log messages
alternatives.why_not: Does not guarantee uniformity of log messages, is error prone and vulnerable to drifting, and provides no value for JSON output.

alternatives.option: Replace klog with another structured logging library
alternatives.why_not: Requires replacing all klog calls, is hard to merge, makes a large share of logs require manual migration, and makes rollback very hard.

alternatives.option: Use glogr instead of the proposed message structure
alternatives.why_not: Glogr serializes both keys and values as JSON, significantly increases log volume, and lacks warning and fatal severity levels.

evidence.quote: add methods to klog to enforce this structure, add ability to configure Kubernetes components to produce logs in JSON format and initiate migration to structured logging
Taking into account the size of Kubernetes repository we will not tackle the problem of full migration to new klog methods but instead focus on improving the querability of most common logs.
We are **not** replacing currently used logging library (klog) or the way in which it is used
Glogr uses JSON serialization for both keys and values
